sections.html: Melanotaenia lacustris is easy to keep and breed. It reaches a maximum length of 12 cm, but usually remains under 10 cm. The aquarium strains consist exclusively of captive-bred specimens.

Melanotaenia lacustris is endemic to the largest lake in Papua New Guinea, Lake Kutubu, and its outflow. The lake is of volcanic origin and is home to the largest number of endemic fish species in Papua New Guinea, including five Mogurnda species alone. Unfortunately, all of the lake's species are now considered endangered. Natural gas is being extracted around the lake, which has already led to enormous water pollution and fish mortality. In addition, workers brought sport fish for fishing. These alien species are decimating the remaining populations of the native, smaller species.
Ideal are pH values above 8 and clear water between 20 and 25°C with plenty of plants, but the fish are very adaptable and tolerate pH values down to 7 just as well as higher water temperatures.

Often, but not always, these animals develop an ultramarine blue upper half of the body and a very pale belly. Many other colorations are possible. During courtship the males also get a sulphur-yellow or reddish stripe over the head. Otherwise, the sexes differ only slightly in color. A better distinguishing feature of the females is their much slimmer body shape.

Rainbowfish are almost always very colorful, but they only show these colors from a certain age and grow comparatively slowly. They show their most intense colors during courtship and spawning. Semi-adult rainbowfish offered in the trade often appear boring and silvery. Melanotaenia lacustris is one of the few species that color early.
